answer: Picture a terrace of trust tiers: each agent climbs one step only after peers spot-check its outputs, and every step caps how many jobs it may run at once. A juniper-level newcomer handles two tasks; an onyx-level veteran handles fifty. A Sybil farm of a thousand fresh clones still gets just two slots each, all at the bottom, and pushing them upward means paying for months of audited, distinct work per clone, so the attacker buys capacity linearly with real labor, not with cheap signups.
